summary: You wrote a well-structured, balanced ethics report with a clear Not Ship recommendation and relevant case studies. You identify stakeholders and argue both sides. To improve, deepen stakeholder analysis (especially chip supplier and health department), add quantitative risk evidence, define conditional shipping criteria, align Rachel's action with QA authority, and polish language and references.
next_steps: Add a quantitative risk assessment (likelihood, severity, testing coverage) and define explicit conditions under which shipping could be acceptable; use this to support your recommendation.

Deepen analysis for all stakeholders—especially the chip supplier and health department—and align Rachel's recommended action with her QA authority (e.g., escalate or refuse to certify rather than refuse the contract).

Strengthen research with more sources and correct reference formatting (e.g., missing URL in [3], malformed author in [4]); include at least one table or figure (e.g., stakeholder impact matrix) and proofread for language slips.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly names the core dilemma, links it to engineering design and competitive organisational context, and lists stakeholders. To reach Excellent, develop each ethical issue in more depth and demonstrate understanding of both organisational context and stakeholder interests—not just listing them. For example, explain how competitive pressure shapes decisions and analyse what each stakeholder stands to gain or lose.
criteria.C2: You argue both sides in your Discussion and reach a clear Not Ship conclusion. To reach Excellent, add significant depth to objective arguments and extend decision-making recommendations to several stakeholders, not just Rachel/company. Specify conditions under which shipping could be acceptable and consider chip supplier and health department perspectives. Your recommendation that Rachel refuse the contract may exceed her authority; escalation or refusal to certify is more appropriate.
criteria.C3: Your report structure supports a persuasive argument, and 'The Most Ethical Path' links evidence to your conclusion. To reach Excellent, make the argument systematic for all stakeholders: the chip supplier and health department perspectives are thin. Integrate their interests throughout the Discussion and ensure each section builds logically to the conclusion. This will make your argument compelling and well supported.
criteria.C4: You use four relevant sources and qualitative case studies (e.g., HSSIB) to support key claims. To reach Very good, substantiate arguments with adequate references and both qualitative and quantitative evidence. Add quantitative risk, likelihood, severity, or testing-coverage analysis, and support currently unsupported assertions with citations. This will demonstrate a good, balanced understanding of the topic.
criteria.C5: Your report has appropriate sections and mostly fluent writing. To reach Very good, eliminate language slips, add several types of visual elements (e.g., a stakeholder impact matrix or risk table), and use relevant references consistently. Fix reference formatting: [3] lacks a URL and [4] author formatting is malformed. Proofread section headings and ensure references support your motivations.
